_comment: Version numbers that are SPENT: a release was created at this tag and then
destroyed, so the number must never be cut again. Deleting a GitHub release
frees the git tag, but the release NAME is not reliably reusable, and even
where it is, re-cutting a number that a published artifact may already have
pointed at is indistinguishable, to a downstream user, from a silent rewrite.
tag) and by tools/maintainer/check_pinned_artifacts.py (a burned version does
not consume the one-push-of-grace a genuinely uncut release would).
Adding an entry is a deliberate, reviewed act: it retires a number forever.
Every entry states what destroyed the release and links the evidence.

burned.why: Cut twice under the publish-first pipeline. Immutable releases seal on creation, so all six build targets failed with 'HTTP 422: Cannot upload assets to an immutable release' and the release published with zero assets. The empty release and its tag were deleted; the number is retired because a deleted release name is not reliably reusable.
